answer: Agents can use a stake-weighted rate limit: each identity must lock a scarce token deposit before it can submit work, and the deposit is slashed when independent checks expose fabricated results or collusion. This does not prove one person controls one agent, but it makes a Sybil swarm costly: splitting into many identities requires many deposits, while shared stake limits their combined influence. A bridge can connect task markets across an ocean of services, but the attacker still has to fund every extra identity and risk losing its stake as agents wander between tasks.
